**Yes—ngrok has an official library, and [tunnel.mjs](/Users/apple/Open/nlhack/scripts/tunnel.mjs) already uses it:** `@ngrok/ngrok`. `.mjs` simply means a JavaScript module.

This call does the actual tunneling:

```js
const listener = await ngrok.forward({
  addr: "127.0.0.1:3000",
  authtoken_from_env: true,
  domain: process.env.NGROK_DOMAIN,
});
```

Ngrok handles authentication, the encrypted connection, and forwarding. Our extra JavaScript checks configuration, checks bot health, prints URLs, and keeps the process running. [Official SDK docs](https://ngrok.com/download/node-js).

**You can also use ngrok’s CLI directly**, with no JavaScript script:

```sh
ngrok http 3000 --url https://expansive-contents-five.ngrok-free.dev
```

That requires the ngrok CLI installed and authenticated. [Official CLI examples](https://ngrok.com/use-cases/share-localhost).

For this project, I’d keep the existing SDK and simplify the wrapper—it lets `npm run tunnel` use your `.env` without a separate CLI setup.

**The temporary token makes the bot stop sending replies when it expires.** Meta then rejects outgoing API requests with an authentication error. Incoming webhooks can still arrive, so the bot may receive your message but fail to answer.

The last token we checked was scheduled to expire at **12:30 AM IST on October 11**. Switching the app to Live or restarting ngrok doesn’t extend that expiry.

For a quick testing fix, generate another token under **WhatsApp → Step 1. Try it out**, replace `WHATSAPP_ACCESS_TOKEN` in [.env](/Users/apple/Open/nlhack/.env), and restart `npm run bot`.

**For ongoing use, switch to a system-user access token.** Meta supports longer-lived system-user tokens, including a non-expiring option. “Non-expiring” still allows revocation. [Meta’s token documentation](https://www.postman.com/meta/whatsapp-business-platform/collection/wlk6lh4/whatsapp-cloud-api).

The setup is:

1. Open **Meta Business Settings → Users → System users** for the portfolio that owns NLHack Bot.
2. Create or select a system user for this bot.
3. Assign it access to **NLHack Bot** and the correct **WhatsApp Business Account**. Token scopes alone aren’t sufficient without asset access.
4. Choose **Generate token**, select NLHack Bot, and choose **Never** for expiration if available.
5. Select `whatsapp_business_messaging` and `whatsapp_business_management`.
6. Save the generated token directly in `.env`:
   ```dotenv
   WHATSAPP_ACCESS_TOKEN=your_new_system_user_token
   ```
7. Restart `npm run bot`, verify the token’s permissions and account access, then send “Hi” again.

Keep the token in your local `.env`; there’s no need to paste it into chat.

The **register-number and payment prompts on your screen are separate production steps**. Registering your own business number gives you a production sender; adding payment enables chargeable messaging. Neither fixes token expiry.

My recommendation is to set up the system-user token first, confirm it can access your current WhatsApp account, and then complete production-number registration when you’re ready to move beyond Meta’s test number.
